summary: The analysis component is the engine's retrieval and search substrate for the perceive stage. It runs three tiers over code: a BM25Index for lexical keyword search, a VectorStore of embedded CodeChunks searched through an HNSW VectorIndex for semantic recall, and a CodeGraph / WorkspaceGraph of GraphNodes and GraphEdges for structural traversal. An ErrorAnalyzer classifies RawErrors into AnalyzedErrors with FixSuggestions, and the tech_debt module scores and prioritizes DebtItems. On the loop it is how the agent finds the right code: chunk, index, search, filter, rank, then feed grounded results into reasoning.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with src/analysis/ read in the context of the full engine under a ~600k budget framing; hybrid lexical/semantic/structural retrieval assumes a large codebase whose relevant slices must be surfaced without loading everything.

examples.title: Chunk source files before indexing anything
examples.intent: Break code into retrievable units with metadata so every index has something coherent to hold.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: chunk_rust splits a file into symbol-aware CodeChunks (falling back to chunk_fixed_size), each stamped with ChunkMetadata, giving the perceive stage the atomic units all three search tiers index.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a file node onto the chunker splits it into a fan of labeled chunk tiles by symbol.
touch_interaction.visual: The file bursts into chunk tiles, each color-tagged by ChunkType (Function blue, Struct green, Test amber).

examples.mini_scenario: The user drags analyzer.rs onto the chunker and chunk_rust fans it into function and impl chunks, each stamped with its line range.
examples.pitfall: Chunk boundaries must preserve line ranges accurately; a chunk whose metadata lines drift makes every later search result cite the wrong location.

examples.title: Build a BM25Index for lexical keyword search
examples.intent: Enable fast exact-term retrieval over symbol names and documented words.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: BM25Index::add_batch ingests chunks (with_params tunes k1/b), tokenizing camelCase and snake_case into term frequencies and IDF, arming the perceive stage with O(fast) keyword lookup.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the lexical node triggers add_batch over the chunk pool; term buckets fill and the IDF table settles.
touch_interaction.visual: A word-cloud of terms condenses into an index grid; the k1/b tuning knobs from with_params sit on the node's rim.

examples.mini_scenario: The user long-presses to index new chunks, and 'getUserName' tokenizes to get/user/name so BM25Index::terms can retrieve it.
examples.pitfall: The IDF and avgdl must be recomputed when documents change; searching a stale index scores terms against outdated frequencies.

examples.title: Query the BM25Index for exact-term hits
examples.intent: Retrieve chunks that contain the query's exact terms, ranked by BM25 score.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: BM25Index::search returns BM25Results (document id plus score) that the perceive stage folds into context; contains and terms let the loop probe index coverage before searching.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the query chip fires it at the lexical index; matching chunk tiles light up in score order.
touch_interaction.visual: Hits glow brighter with their BM25 score; a small badge shows the result count from the search.

examples.mini_scenario: A query for 'find_cycles' hits the exact symbol via BM25Index::search even when the semantic index ranks unrelated graph code higher.
examples.pitfall: BM25 only matches terms it has seen; a query word absent from the index vocabulary returns nothing regardless of relevance.

examples.title: Rebuild the lexical index after files change
examples.intent: Keep keyword search honest as the codebase mutates under the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: BM25Index::remove drops a stale document and rebuild recomputes the whole statistics table, letting the control layer schedule re-indexing between loop turns instead of mid-search.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a stale chunk tile off the index removes its document; a rebuild badge appears when drift accumulates.
touch_interaction.visual: The tile greys out and slides off the grid; the index node shows a pulsing 'rebuild' badge until statistics settle.

examples.mini_scenario: After the agent rewrites config.rs, the control step removes its old chunks and rebuild runs before the next perceive turn.
examples.pitfall: Removing documents without rebuilding leaves IDF stale; interleaving remove and search across loop turns yields inconsistent scores.

examples.title: Embed chunks into the VectorStore with a backend
examples.intent: Turn code chunks into vectors so meaning-based recall becomes possible.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VectorStore::add_chunk embeds each CodeChunk through the configured EmbeddingBackend (with_api_key arms the Http backend) and inserts the normalized vector into the HNSW VectorIndex.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a chunk sends it through add_chunk; a vector trail flows into the HNSW node.
touch_interaction.visual: The chunk emits a shimmering vector arrow that threads into the index sphere, which pulses as it inserts.

examples.mini_scenario: With the Http backend configured via with_api_key, the user taps a batch of chunks and their embeddings stream into the HNSW index.
examples.pitfall: Embedding dimension must match the index; feeding vectors from a different backend dimension into an existing VectorIndex corrupts search.

examples.title: Search the VectorIndex for the k nearest chunks
examples.intent: Retrieve the chunks whose meaning is closest to the query, not just its words.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VectorStore::search embeds the query and runs HNSW k-NN ranked by cosine_similarity, returning scored chunks the perceive stage folds into context.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading from the query node radiates a similarity field; the nearest chunk tiles pull toward it.
touch_interaction.visual: Chunks arrange by cosine_similarity in concentric rings; the closest glow bright, distant ones fade.

examples.mini_scenario: A query about retry logic returns the three nearest chunks by cosine similarity even though none contain the word 'retry'.
examples.pitfall: Score derives from distance, not raw distance; treating HNSW distance as relevance inverts the ranking and surfaces the least similar chunks.

examples.title: Apply a SearchFilter to scope results
examples.intent: Restrict search to relevant files, chunk types, languages, or a min score.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A SearchFilter built with with_file_pattern, with_chunk_type, with_language and with_min_score narrows candidates via matches before ranking, so the perceive stage only ingests chunks that pass the scope.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the results panel opens filter chips; toggling one dims out chunks that fail matches.
touch_interaction.visual: Filter chips (Function, *.rs, score>0.5) light when active; failing chunks grey out and drop from the stack.

examples.mini_scenario: The user filters to Function chunks in src/ with min_score above 0.6, cutting a noisy result set to five precise hits.
examples.pitfall: A min_score set too high can empty the result set; over-filtering starves reasoning of context it needed to answer.

examples.title: Weight chunks by type and tags before final rank
examples.intent: Prefer higher-signal chunk kinds when two results score similarly.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ChunkType::weight (Function outranks Import) multiplies raw similarity, and metadata set via with_symbol/with_tag sharpens matchability, so the reason stage ranks a matching function above a matching import at equal cosine.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the ranking dial re-weights by ChunkType; function tiles climb the list while imports sink.
touch_interaction.visual: Tiles reshuffle as their weight badges apply; the list reorders with a smooth vertical slide.

examples.mini_scenario: Two chunks tie on similarity; the type weight lifts the Function above the Comment so it ranks first in context.
examples.pitfall: Type weight should nudge, not dominate; over-weighting can bury a highly relevant comment that actually answers the query.

examples.title: Fuse BM25 and vector scores into a hybrid rank
examples.intent: Get the precision of keyword match plus the recall of semantic similarity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The reason stage merges BM25Results from BM25Index::search with scored chunks from VectorStore::search, so a chunk strong on either exact terms or meaning surfaces, widening what the loop can find.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the lexical and semantic result columns together merges them into one fused ranking.
touch_interaction.visual: Two colored streams (blue lexical, green semantic) braid into a single ranked column with blended tile borders.

examples.mini_scenario: A query for 'BM25Index' hits exactly via lexical and its callers via semantic; fusion returns both the definition and its usages.
examples.pitfall: Normalize the two score scales before fusing; adding raw BM25 to cosine lets one metric silently swamp the other.

examples.title: Soft-delete a chunk and compact when the index degrades
examples.intent: Remove stale chunks from results without an expensive index rebuild, then sweep when health drops.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VectorStore::remove_chunk and remove_file mark entries deleted and rebuild_id_index keeps lookups coherent; the control layer calls compact only when check_health or verify_index_integrity reports the index has degraded.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a chunk tile off the canvas marks it deleted; a health gauge on the index node ticks toward the compaction line.
touch_interaction.visual: The tile fades to a ghost outline; the index node's health ring shifts green to amber as deletions accumulate.

examples.mini_scenario: A refactored file's chunks are removed via remove_file; they vanish from results while compact waits for check_health to signal real degradation.
examples.pitfall: Compact when integrity checks say so, not on a whim; compacting after every delete stalls the loop on rebuilds it did not need.

examples.title: Triage compiler output into prioritized AnalyzedErrors
examples.intent: Turn raw compiler output into categorized, ordered errors the loop can act on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ErrorAnalyzer::analyze maps each RawError to an AnalyzedError with an ErrorCategory and priority; analyze_batch, group_by_category and first_to_fix give the perceive stage an ordered queue instead of a wall of text.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a raw error line classifies it into a category chip and slots it into the priority lane.
touch_interaction.visual: The error line snaps a category badge (BorrowError red, StyleWarning grey) and drops into the lane first_to_fix would pop.

examples.mini_scenario: A cargo build fails; analyze tags an E0502 as a borrow error at high priority so first_to_fix surfaces it before a style warning.
examples.pitfall: Category drives priority; misclassifying a blocking type error as a style warning lets the loop skip past a fatal error.

examples.title: Emit a FixSuggestion the loop can gate on
examples.intent: Propose a concrete fix and mark whether it is safe to apply automatically.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each AnalyzedError carries a FixSuggestion whose confidence and auto-fix flag let the reason stage decide between applying a safe fix directly and routing a risky one to review before the act stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing an error reveals its fix card with a confidence meter and an auto-fix toggle.
touch_interaction.visual: The fix card unfolds; a green auto-fix badge shows when the suggestion is auto-fixable, the confidence bar filling proportionally.

examples.mini_scenario: An unused import gets a high-confidence auto-fixable suggestion applied silently, while a lifetime fix routes to operator review.
examples.pitfall: Only auto-apply high-confidence suggestions; auto-applying a low-confidence structural fix can compile away real intent.

examples.title: Build the CodeGraph of nodes and typed edges
examples.intent: Represent the codebase as a traversable structure so structural queries become possible.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: add_node and add_edge (or connect) assemble GraphNodes via add_file/add_module/add_function/add_struct/add_trait, linked by typed GraphEdges, giving the foundation layer a structure beside the text indices.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading over the codebase node expands it into a live node-and-edge graph laid out by dependency.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes settle into a force-directed layout; call edges thin blue, import edges dashed, implement edges bold arrows.

examples.mini_scenario: The user spreads the graph and sees the call structure of the vector_store module render as connected function nodes.
examples.pitfall: Edge types must reflect real relations; a fabricated call edge corrupts every path query built on the graph.

examples.title: Walk dependencies and dependents from one node
examples.intent: See what a symbol uses and what uses it before touching it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: From a node found by get_node_by_id, outgoing_edges/incoming_edges and the dependencies/dependents helpers give the perceive stage the immediate structural neighborhood around a change target.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a node fans out its dependencies on one side and its dependents on the other.
touch_interaction.visual: Outbound edges slide left in blue, inbound edges right in amber; the focus node holds center with a bright ring.

examples.mini_scenario: The user double-taps VectorStore::search and sees its callees on the left and every module that calls it on the right.
examples.pitfall: Dependents change as the graph rebuilds; caching a dependents list across an edit turn acts on stale impact data.

examples.title: Find a path between two GraphNodes
examples.intent: Discover how one code entity reaches another through the dependency structure.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph::find_path runs BFS over GraphEdges between two GraphNodes, giving the reason stage the concrete chain linking a caller to a callee.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing from one node to another traces the shortest edge path; the route highlights hop by hop.
touch_interaction.visual: A glowing path lights the intermediate nodes and edges; off-path nodes dim to focus the route.

examples.mini_scenario: The user draws from a public API node to a private helper and find_path highlights the three-hop call chain between them.
examples.pitfall: BFS finds a shortest path, not the only one; presenting it as the sole route hides other dependency chains that also matter.

examples.title: Detect cycles in the CodeGraph
examples.intent: Flag circular dependencies that signal fragile architecture.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph::find_cycles surfaces circular GraphEdge chains, letting the verify stage reject or warn on structures that would tangle the dependency order.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the graph runs a cycle sweep; any loop of edges lights red and its nodes pulse together.
touch_interaction.visual: A detected cycle rings its nodes in red and animates the loop direction with a rotating dashed edge.

examples.mini_scenario: The verify stage runs find_cycles before a merge and flags a new A-to-B-to-A import loop for the human to break.
examples.pitfall: A cycle in test-only edges may be acceptable; treating every cycle as fatal blocks harmless mutual references.

examples.title: Rank hub nodes by graph metrics
examples.intent: Find the most-connected entities that a change would ripple through.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph::node_metrics computes per-node degree and find_hubs ranks the top GraphNodes, so the reason stage knows which entities are high-impact before proposing a change near them; subgraph can isolate a hub's region.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching on the graph rescales each node by its degree; hubs swell large while leaves shrink to dots.
touch_interaction.visual: Node sizes rescale to degree; the biggest hubs glow warm and cast the most edges.

examples.mini_scenario: The user pinches and sees the VectorStore node swell as the largest hub, warning that touching it ripples widely.
examples.pitfall: Degree measures coupling, not importance; a high-degree utility may be safe to change while a low-degree core type is not.

examples.title: Summarize a WorkspaceGraph around a focus symbol
examples.intent: Retrieve a bounded structural neighborhood around one symbol of interest.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: build_workspace_graph assembles the workspace-wide graph and summarize_graph applies WorkspaceGraphOptions (focus, depth, node cap) to produce a WorkspaceGraphSummary, giving the perceive stage a size-capped subgraph.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching around a focus node crops the graph to its neighborhood at the chosen depth.
touch_interaction.visual: The graph fades to grey except the focus and its depth-N neighbors, which stay sharp within a lens circle.

examples.mini_scenario: The user pinches around VectorStore at depth 2 and summarize_graph returns its callers, callees, and their types capped at the node limit.
examples.pitfall: Respect the node cap in WorkspaceGraphOptions; an unbounded neighborhood around a hub expands to the whole workspace and blows the budget.

examples.title: Prioritize tech debt into a roadmap
examples.intent: Rank technical debt so the loop fixes the highest-value items first.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The tech_debt module scores each DebtItem — total_cost compounds fix_cost with monthly_interest, severity_weight scales impact, and hotspot_score folds in churn_rate — then prioritize and generate_roadmap order the work for the reason stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the debt list re-sorts it by priority_score; the costliest items rise to the top.
touch_interaction.visual: Debt cards re-order by score; high-interest items carry a rising cost curve, security items a red shield accent.

examples.mini_scenario: The user flicks the debt list and a high-churn file with mounting monthly_interest jumps to the top of the generated roadmap.
examples.pitfall: The strategy changes the order, not the debt; sorting by effort alone can bury a critical security item that severity_weight would surface.

examples.title: Render the graph to a shareable diagram
examples.intent: Export the structural graph as a diagram a human can read and reason over.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeGraph::render and render_to emit DOT, Mermaid, ASCII, or PlantUML (cluster and with_direction shape layout), and render_workspace_graph does the same at workspace scale, letting the act stage produce a human-facing artifact from the structure the loop reasons on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the graph exports it via render_to in the selected format; a rendered diagram card slides out.
touch_interaction.visual: A format chip (Mermaid/DOT) highlights and a clean rendered diagram peels off the live graph as a shareable card.

examples.mini_scenario: The user double-taps to export the module graph as Mermaid for a design doc, matching the graph the agent searched.
examples.pitfall: Rendering must reflect the current graph; exporting a cached diagram after the graph re-scanned ships a picture that lies about the code.
